title: Test run buried in repeated tool-output spam, then a real CI-speed decision
notes: Deliberately contains long runs of near-identical tool-output lines (simulating verbose CI/test logs). Tests whether the extractor produces one clean fact/decision set instead of one junk atom per repeated line, and whether the cleanup stage's repeated-line dedup helps or the extractor still overproduces.

All green — 40 test files, 612 tests passed.
Great. While that ran, I noticed the CI job takes 11 minutes now, up from 4 minutes last month. Any idea why?

Looking at the CI config — someone added --reporter=verbose globally which triggers full stack traces even on pass, and more importantly the job isn't using vitest's cache directory between runs (.vitest-cache isn't in the CI cache key). I'd add that to the cache key and drop the global verbose reporter.

Updated CI config: added .vitest-cache to the cache key path, removed --reporter=verbose from the default run (kept it available via a manual workflow_dispatch flag for debugging). Should get us most of the way back toward 4 minutes.

gold_atoms.text: The test suite passed: 40 test files, 612 tests, all green.
CI job duration grew from about 4 minutes to about 11 minutes over the last month.
CI wasn't caching vitest's .vitest-cache directory between runs, and a global --reporter=verbose flag was forcing full stack traces even on passing tests — both were inflating CI time.
Add .vitest-cache to the CI cache key and remove the global --reporter=verbose flag, keeping verbose output available via a manual workflow_dispatch flag.
